title: Town of Savoy Incorporation Charter — Fannin County, Texas, May 1885
text:
State of Texas          In Vacation   May 16th 1885
Fannin County } Whereas the Town of Savoy has been duly
& legally incorporated under the provisions of Chapter 11 Title
XVII of the Revised Statutes of the State of Texas by an order
duly made on the Records of the Commissioners Court of
Fannin County on the 6th day of May 1885 by the County Judge
of said County. Now Therefor I C. D. McClellan County Judge
of Fannin County Texas by virtue of the Authority vested in
me by Texas And in Compliance with Article 410 Chapter
11 Title XVII of said Revised Statutes, do hereby order that
an Election be held at Rugstalio[?] Store house in said Town
of Savoy by the qualified Voters of said Town on Saturday
the 30th day of May 1885 for the purpose of Electing a Mayor,
a Marshall And five Aldermen for said Town. And I hereby
appoint W. A. Youree presiding Officer of said Election and a
Certified Copy of this order Shall be evidence of his Authority in
the premises.
Witness My hand this May 16th 1885.

[Page 2 — Charter/Incorporation document:]
State of Texas }
Fannin County } Be it remembered that
whereas an election was held in the Town of Savoy
in Fannin County, Texas, on the 4th[?] day of May
A.D. 1885, by the qualified voters thereof in pursuance of
law and an order duly made by the County Judge
of said County to determine whether or not said Town
should be incorporated under the provisions of Chapter
Eleven Title Seventeen of the Revised Statutes of Texas,
and whereas at said Election a majority of all votes
cast were for Incorporation.
Now therefore I, C. D. McClellan County Judge of
Fannin County Texas by virtue of the authority
vested in me by Texas, do hereby declare and order
that the inhabitants of said Town of Savoy &
residing within the following boundaries be and
the same are hereby incorporated under the corporate
Name "Town of Savoy" — The boundaries of said
Town shall extend one fourth mile North, South,
East and West from the North East corner of
Lot No. in Block No. 428, upon which the Post Office
building is situated in said Town.
In witness whereof I have hereunto
set my Official Signature this the 6th day of May
A.D. 1885.
D. McClellan,
County Judge,
Fannin County, Texas.
notes: Document appears to contain two related pages: (1) an election order dated May 16, 1885 calling for an incorporation election on May 30, 1885; and (2) the actual incorporation declaration signed May 6, 1885 by County Judge D. McClellan (also written as C. D. McClellan). The store name where the election was to be held is difficult to read — possibly 'Rugstalio' or similar. Lot number in Block No. 428 is blank in the original. Handwritten cursive throughout.
